articles.title: Commander Shepard’s Actors Are ‘Wildly Hopeful’ for Mass Effect, Despite Everything
articles.summary: Fans have tangled with a mix of emotions knowing that it’s unlikely they’ll ever get to play a new BioWare-developed Mass Effect again. But, if you ask the voices of Commander Shepard, they’re oddly optimistic about the future despite the circumstances.
body: EA shut down BioWare, laid off its staff, and canceled the in-development Mass Effect: Universe in October. That news sent shockwaves throughout the industry and through the communities that have sprung up around BioWare’s games. Mass Effect fans were hit particularly hard, and have started a petition to save Mass Effect. Some even purchased a time on a billboard in Times Square to advertise it.
“My first response was sadness and concern for everybody who worked at Bioware,” Meer said.

After gutting the studio a year ago, EA laid off BioWare’s remaining around 50 employees on Oct. 21, bringing an end to its 30-year legacy. Meer noted that BioWare was a source of pride in Canada, and especially in Edmonton, where the studio was based. Canadian fans are even petitioning their government to save BioWare, and that petition will be presented in the House of Commons, meaning the Canadian government will formally address it in some way. “They were such a force in gaming and they were such a legend,” Meer said.
points: Fans have tangled with a mix of emotions knowing that it’s unlikely they’ll ever get to play a new BioWare-developed Mass Effect again.
But, if you ask the voices of Commander Shepard, they’re oddly optimistic about the future despite the circumstances.

articles.title: Wardogs Season 3 brings an urban map, Limited Mode, and a 185,000-account ban wave
articles.summary: Wardogs' Season 3 will launch on 12th November, complete with a new urban map, a new Limited Mode, and a ban wave targeting 185,000 accounts.
body: Developer Bulkhead confirmed the details earlier this week, revealing plans for a full wipe and progression changes that it hopes will "recapture the shared discovery and sense of achievement that defined" the 100-player tactical shooter when it first launched in Early Access.

The new map will focus on close-quarters fighting, and for a "more level playing field", players can dip into Limited Mode, which offers "an alternative way to experience" the game as it restricts weapons, ammunition, armour, and vehicles.
While the full list of restrictions is still being decided, it currently includes FMJ-only ammunition, a Tier 2 armour cap, and a reduced attack vehicle selection.
"The mode is designed to preserve the feel of early-to-mid-game combat and reduce the advantage offered by more powerful equipment," the team said.
points: Wardogs' Season 3 will launch on 12th November, complete with a new urban map, a new Limited Mode, and a ban wave targeting 185,000 accounts.

articles.title: Wardogs Season 3 Will Add A Mode That Limits What Weapons Players Can Use
articles.summary: Bulkhead and Team17 shared the first details on what players can expect from Wardogs Season 3 in a new video. One of the most notable additions is Limited Mode, a new way to play Wardogs that restricts what weapons and other upgrades players have access to.
body: In its Road to Season 3 video, Bulkhead explains that it learned from the backlash towards Season 2 and will now mostly stick to its own vision for the game rather than overreacting to the loudest demands from the community. As part of the adjustments, progression is being brought back more in line with Season 1, and Wardogs ' seasons will now last three months.

While a major meta-game progression overhaul is happening in 2027, Wardogs is introducing multi-track unlocks in the meantime, meaning that some items are no longer locked to a specific progression track. It's also part of why Bulkhead is introducing Limited Mode servers, so players don't feel outclassed simply because they haven't gotten as far through the in-game progression as other players.

On Limited Mode servers, players will be restricted to certain weaponry and ammo types, only be able to use up to tier-2 armor, and not have access to certain vehicles. Cash and XP earned in Limited Mode can be spent in the standard game mode, so it's probably what players new to the game will want to check out first in Season 3.

articles.title: Path of Exile 2 Sets The Stage For Massive Update Alongside December Launch
articles.summary: At ExileCon 2026, Grinding Gear Games gave us a deep dive into everything we can expect to be added to Path of Exile 2 by the time its 1.0 launch happens next month. That includes a new stealth-driven class, two more narrative acts for its campaign, and a new league called Conquerors of Wraeclast.
body: The most obvious thing that Path of Exile 2's 1.0 launch will do is wrap up the main campaign with Acts 5 and 6. This will exponentially increase the amount of content in the game, with a press release teasing that 24 new areas and 18 new bosses will come to the game as part of these final two acts. Players will also now have access to a new stealth-driven Shadow class, which lets players lay traps on the battlefield, chain kills to keep reset their stealth cooldown time, and summon Shades to fight alongside them.

If you just want to boot up Path of Exile 2 and play through its campaign, 1.0 seems like the time to do so. For those who plan on sticking around after finishing the campaign, there are a lot of other things for you to look forward to in the endgame. For example, Shadow has two new Ascendancy classes, the Assassin and the Infiltrator. Meanwhile, the Duelist class gains the Knight Ascendancy, which gives them access to a squire companion and other new abilities.
points: At ExileCon 2026, Grinding Gear Games gave us a deep dive into everything we can expect to be added to Path of Exile 2 by the time its 1.0 launch happens next month.

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero: Where Is the Rest of Godzilla’s Rogues' Gallery?
articles.summary: Where is the rest of Godzilla’s rogues' gallery? We take a look at Monster Island's most wanted.
body: Godzilla Minus Zero is upon us, and going by the reviews, it looks like the venerable kaiju franchise has another winner on its hands. More than 70 years after his debut, Godzilla continues to be one of the most iconic characters in cinema history. But even though Minus Zero is another strong entry for the King of the Monsters, I couldn’t help but be a little disappointed that the movie continues a frustrating trend that’s plagued the last couple decades of Godzilla movies by only featuring a handful of his monster co-stars.

Specifically, King Ghidorah is the antagonist of Minus Zero, once again assuming his role as the Big G’s archenemy. Now, I love King Ghidorah, but the alien dragon takes up a lot of oxygen in Toho’s filmography, and there is a deep bench of Godzilla friends and foes who haven’t shown up in years. Let’s look into how the Godzilla franchise isn’t using its roster of monsters to their full potential.

articles.title: Linux on the desktop marches on as GOG announces its Galaxy client is getting a revamp headed to Windows, macOS, and your distro of choice
articles.summary: GOG Galaxy—the DRM-free storefront's go at a desktop client and launcher—was always a nice dream that didn't measure up in reality. The pitch was: all your games, from all your PC game storefronts, in one centralised hub, but it never left beta in its 2.0 form and, in general, ran pretty poorly…
body: But that was old GOG. New, independent GOG has big plans for Galaxy. In the storefront's first "GOG Showcase", released Thursday, it announced the launcher would be getting a revamp in 2027, and it's coming to Linux too. "We know this has been a long time coming, but we wanted to do it properly: GOG Galaxy is officially heading to Linux", says the studio.

"At the same time, we’ve reworked the client on Windows and Mac to be simpler, run faster, and give you cleaner ways to view your library. Most importantly, our core promise stays untouched: GOG Galaxy is entirely optional. Your games are yours to download and keep through offline installers, exactly as they’ve always been".
That is to say, you'll still be able to find offline game installers in your GOG library if you want to prep for the digital ownership apocalypse (which, let me be clear, is probably a wise move).

articles.title: Mass Effect composer Sam Hulick releases his 're-scored' trailer for N7 Day, 'my way of saying goodbye… at least for now'
articles.summary: Hulick also revealed that he was asked by BioWare to score an internal demo for Mass Effect: Universe—but work was cut short by the studio's closure.
body: Mass Effect composer Sam Hulick revealed in October that he was 're-scoring' the leaked trailer for Mass Effect: Universe to reflect his own "musical vision" for the game. The original, with an edit of " Quartz " by French 79, is pretty groovy, but now Hulick's work is done and this may not come as much of a surprise but I think I like his version better.

I'm not a music critic but I know what I like, and I really like the Mass Effect soundtracks. There's a broadly common sound threaded through all three games (I didn't play Andromeda so I'm just pretending it never happened) but they evolved over the course of the trilogy, too: Hulick told me his music in this trailer is "'a balancing act between paying homage to the original trilogy and exploring new ground", but leans most heavily toward Mass Effect 1 and 3.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever World First Level 60 Character Hits Cap Three Days After Launch
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever is all about taking your time and exploring the world, rather than rushing to the endgame. But, despite the Forever team's insistence on taking your time and making friends, a WoW Forever player has already hit level 60.
body: Team JokerD, led by the eponymous streamer was the first team of characters to hit level 60, and the team was made up entirely of Undead characters and one Troll. The Undead race was important there, because Blizzard changed the Cannibalize ability to help you regenerate mana, which meant there was little to no downtime between massive pulls. I spent some time watching the streams of these speedrunners, and they'd gather entire groups of mobs to nuke them down with AoE abilities.

JokerD's claim to fame was being the world's first level 60 when World of Warcraft Classic launched back in 2019, so it's not super suprising that his team was the first to hit max level in Forever. There was plenty of competition this time around, but JokerD's team was pretty far ahead of the fray throughout the entire race. Even at the time of writing, the second place character who's not part of JokerD's team is Ksuper Worldfirst, who is still level 53.

articles.title: Todd Howard's game design power is knowing when to make things 'simple and digestible' according to Skyrim's lead designer
articles.summary: Todd Howard is one of the most recognisable names in game development, yet despite this, the Bethesda director's overarching thoughts on game design remain something of an enigma. Howard has admitted that he doesn't like talking about his games.
body: "Part of what Todd has, historically for Skyrim and Fallout 3 and everything, been very good at is putting himself in the seat of your typical player," Nesmith explained. "As a developer, I sit in an ivory tower. It's inescapable … I think more deeply about games, definitely, than your typical player. And he's able to cut through that and see 'Oh yeah, they're looking for a little bit of joy here. Don't get in the way with your math and your complex decision here'".

Nesmith clarifies that this isn't Howard's only talent and that he "thinks very deeply about games", while Nesmith himself can also "think from the player['s perspective]. But he says that both designers had a "bias" to see things from a particular direction, and in game development, it's often good to "find other people who have a counterbias to bounce your ideas off of so that you can get the well-rounded opinion."

articles.title: Xbox is testing a way to use your phone as a controller on smart TVs
articles.summary: Xbox is testing two new ways to play its cloud games, and one of them doesn't require a controller at all.
body: Announced on Xbox Wire on 4th November, the phone controller preview is rolling out on supported TVs wherever Xbox Cloud Gaming is available. The phone option - which works with both Android and iOS devices - lets you use your phone "as a controller when you don't have one nearby". Connect to your TV via QR code, and the controls open in your phone's browser.

The second preview, called cloud connect, is currently limited to the US and lets the new Xbox Nano controller talk to your cloud session over wi- fi instead of pairing directly with your TV to "help reduce input latency, so gameplay feels more responsive".
To try out the phone controls yourself, switch on Preview Features under Settings > Account in the latest version of the Xbox smart TV app.

Xbox has published a setup guide with full instructions, although you should note that both experiences "are still being tested", so the availability and supported games or devices "may be limited while [Xbox] learns from your feedback".
points: Xbox is testing two new ways to play its cloud games, and one of them doesn't require a controller at all.

articles.title: What we've been playing - "Sniffing out the warehouses on Prawn Island"
articles.summary: Well, hello! I am once again wearing the Bertie hat in your usual host's absence, so joyous welcomes to our regular feature in which we talk about what we've been playing in recent times.
body: But enough about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Do tell all! And don't forget we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your leisurely perusal, just in case you forgot what you were playing a year or a month or a week ago. Bye!

Once again, I am finally playing a game from my backlog that I should've played years ago, and that's the delightful albeit dark card game Inscryption. There's so much more to this than you'd first expect, and I'm surprised the community has been able to keep the game's best bits under wraps for so long. Ultimately, nothing could've prepared me for Act 2, and my only real qualm with the whole experience is that I wish Act 2 had its own endless roguelike mode; you'd never be able to pull me away from it.

The game falters a little at the start of Act 3, I'll admit, and I've found myself very frustrated by what is an otherwise relatively easy time. This is down to me missing some rather useful earlier cards that I've since learnt would've made this final stretch much breezier, but oh well. I will still take down the Uberbots one way or another for the love of the game!

articles.title: After furloughing its developers and then hiring some of them back, Star Wars Zero Company developer has laid off an unspecified number of staff
articles.summary: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid of an unspecified number of developers, after furloughing its entire team and then hiring some of that staff back.
body: As reported by the Star Wars website Bespin Bulletin, several designers of the acclaimed tactics game have taken to LinkedIn to announce that they have been let go by the studio. Among those affected are senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who worked on the game for three and a half years and has been on furlough for the past three and a half months.
"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote in a LinkedIn post.

Other designers who lost their jobs include UI Engineer Tyler Eichten and senior quality assurance analyst Ryan Mosher, who spent two years at Firaxis and a further two years at 1047 Games before joining Bit Reactor in October 2024.

videos.title: Want a New Elder Scrolls? Play Queen's Domain, the Old-School RPG Inspired by King's Field
videos.summary: Queen's Domain impressions by Michael Higham, played on PC (also available on PS5, Xbox, and Switch 2)
body: "I'm a sucker for a good throwback to the early polygonal 32-bit era – Mouthwashing, Signalis, Crow Country, and Boltgun 2 are some recent favorites that come to mind. The latest one I've locked in on is Queen's Domain, a fantasy RPG that's as if an Elder Scrolls game was made for the PlayStation 1. Actually, it's explicitly inspired by FromSoftware's pre-Dark Souls series King's Field, where slow, deliberate first-person combat and exploration complemented punishing difficulty (which would later become FromSoft's signature, of course). But as much as Queen's Domain draws clear inspiration or shares similarities, it's a singular experience in 2026 that, from what I've played so far, wields the intended friction of an old-school game wonderfully."
